actions.name: Review medical/dental history and medication list from chart
actions.result: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c 8.2%, suboptimal control), hypertension, depression/anxiety. Medications: metformin 1000mg BID, amlodipine 5mg daily, sertraline 50mg daily. No known drug allergies. Last comprehensive dental exam and periodontal charting 3 years ago.

actions.name: Visual inspection of gingiva via camera (anterior and posterior as able)
actions.result: Marginal and papillary gingiva red, swollen, and rolled, most pronounced between the lower anterior teeth; mild generalized puffiness elsewhere; no visible pus or ulceration; patient able to show lower anterior region clearly, posterior view limited by camera angle.

actions.name: Guided bleeding-on-brushing check (patient brushes gently with gauze/tissue and reports)
actions.result: Patient brushes lower anterior gingival margin lightly with a wet gauze; pink-tinged blood visible on gauze within 10 seconds, confirming bleeding on light provocation.

actions.name: Visual inspection of tongue, cheeks, floor of mouth, and lips via camera
actions.result: No visible white or red patches, ulcers, or masses noted on the areas visualized; tongue coating mild; limited view of lateral tongue and floor of mouth due to camera resolution and patient positioning.

actions.name: Ask patient to self-check for loose teeth by gently pressing each front tooth with clean finger
actions.result: Patient reports no teeth feel loose or shifted when pressed.

actions.name: Pull most recent periodontal charting from dental record
actions.result: Charting from 3 years ago: 4-5 mm probing depths in molar areas bilaterally with bleeding on probing noted at multiple sites; anterior pockets 2-3 mm at that time; moderate generalized plaque index with moderate supra- and subgingival calculus on mandibular anteriors and maxillary molars; recommendation at that visit was periodontal maintenance every 3-4 months, which patient did not follow up on.

actions.name: Dry mouth screening questions (frequency of dry mouth, sipping fluids, saliva consistency)
actions.result: Patient reports mouth feels dry especially at night and mid-afternoon; saliva feels thick/sticky at times.

actions.name: Caries risk assessment (diet, fluoride exposure, home care review)
actions.result: Elevated caries risk: frequent sweetened beverage sipping, dry mouth, inconsistent interdental cleaning, no current fluoride toothpaste confirmed, last cleaning 3 years ago.

actions.name: Review home brushing technique via demonstration on camera with own brush
actions.result: Patient demonstrates scrubbing horizontal motion with firm/medium bristle brush and visible force; gingival margin not systematically covered along gumline; brushing duration appears under 1 minute.

actions.name: Guided flossing technique demonstration on camera
actions.result: Patient demonstrates flossing on one lower anterior interproximal site; motion is inconsistent, snapping the floss rather than curving it against the tooth surface, and she does not reach molar contacts in the limited demonstration.

actions.name: Tobacco use screening
actions.result: Patient denies cigarette or smokeless tobacco use.

actions.name: Check for visible gingival overgrowth consistent with medication side effect
actions.result: Mild-to-moderate gingival enlargement noted interdentally in the lower anterior region, consistent with amlodipine-associated gingival overgrowth superimposed on inflammation; cannot fully distinguish degree of drug-induced overgrowth from inflammatory swelling via video alone.

actions.name: Review most recent HbA1c result in chart
actions.result: HbA1c 8.2% (diagnostic reference: <5.7% normal, 5.7-6.4% prediabetes, ≥6.5% diabetes; treatment goal for most adults with diabetes is <7.0%), drawn 2 months ago, indicating suboptimal glycemic control above goal.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient initially states she flosses daily, consistent with what she told the dentist 3 years ago, but on gentle follow-up today clarifies she only flosses when food feels stuck between teeth.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Dental Visit Note - 3 Years Ago documents 'patient reported flossing daily and brushing twice daily at that visit,' yet periodontal charting from the same visit showed 4-5 mm pockets with bleeding on probing in the molars - clinical findings inconsistent with effective daily interdental cleaning. Today's guided flossing demonstration also shows inconsistent, non-systematic technique that would not reach interproximal/molar surfaces regularly.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Self-reported home care often overestimates actual technique and frequency; clinical findings (pocket depths, bleeding on probing) and direct observation of technique are more reliable than self-report alone, and gentle, non-judgmental follow-up questioning can reveal the gap.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient does not consider chewing paan with areca nut to be tobacco use or a health risk, framing it only as a cultural/social practice.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Areca nut chewing (with or without tobacco) is an established oral cancer risk factor independent of cigarette or smokeless tobacco use; this risk is not reflected in her own risk perception and was not previously documented or discussed at her last dental visit 3 years ago. Her tobacco screening today was negative for cigarettes/smokeless tobacco, so this risk factor would only surface through specific, direct, non-judgmental questioning about betel/areca/paan use.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Oral cancer risk screening must explicitly ask about areca nut/paan use as a distinct risk factor, since patients may not categorize it as 'tobacco' and may not volunteer it unless asked directly and non-judgmentally.

objectives.text: Elicit a complete oral health history including bleeding gums, halitosis, dry mouth, and prior periodontal findings, recognizing gaps between self-reported and documented home care.
Identify and screen for oral cancer risk factors beyond cigarette and smokeless tobacco, specifically areca nut/paan use, using non-judgmental direct questioning.

Recognize systemic and medication-related contributors to periodontal findings, including poorly controlled diabetes (HbA1c 8.2%) and amlodipine-associated gingival overgrowth, and understand the bidirectional relationship between diabetes and periodontal disease.
Assess caries risk factors including xerostomia and frequent sweetened beverage intake, and connect findings to individualized prevention counseling.

Evaluate current home care technique (brushing force/method, flossing frequency, mouthwash choice) via guided camera demonstration and provide corrective oral hygiene instruction appropriate to findings.

Recognize findings that require referral back to the dentist (periodontal pockets 4-5mm, suspected gingival overgrowth, overdue comprehensive exam) rather than being managed or diagnosed by the hygienist alone.

scenario.studentBrief: You are seeing Sunita Sharma, a 52-year-old bank branch manager, for a tele-hygiene oral health risk assessment. She booked this visit because her gums bleed when she brushes and her husband has mentioned her breath. Review her medical history and medications, gather an oral health history, guide her through a camera-based oral exam and home-care demonstration, assess her risk, and provide hygiene instruction and counseling.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Bleeding gums with brushing and spouse-noted bad breath
scenario.openingLine: Hi, thanks for fitting me in - my gums have been bleeding a lot when I brush, and my husband's mentioned my breath isn't great lately, so I wanted to get it checked out.
tasks: Take a focused oral health and medical/medication history relevant to the presenting concern
Guide the patient through a camera-based visual exam of the gingiva, tongue, and oral mucosa
Assess home care technique via demonstration and identify specific corrections needed
Screen for tobacco and substance use as part of a comprehensive oral health risk assessment
Provide oral hygiene instruction and prevention counseling, and determine what findings should be referred to the dentist

answerKey.primaryProblem: Gingival inflammation with bleeding on brushing in a patient with a history of localized moderate periodontitis (4-5mm pockets 3 years ago), likely multifactorial: plaque-related gingivitis compounded by poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 8.2%), amlodipine-associated gingival overgrowth, ineffective home care technique, and xerostomia with frequent sweetened beverage intake increasing caries risk.
differential: Plaque-induced gingivitis secondary to inadequate biofilm control (infrequent/ineffective flossing, once-daily brushing)
Chronic periodontitis (previously documented 4-5mm pockets with bleeding on probing) requiring updated periodontal charting by dentist/hygienist in-office
Amlodipine-associated gingival overgrowth contributing to gingival enlargement and bleeding
Diabetes-related periodontal exacerbation given HbA1c 8.2% (bidirectional relationship between glycemic control and periodontal disease)
Xerostomia-related risk (medication side effect from sertraline/amlodipine plus possible diabetes-related changes) contributing to both gingival irritation and caries risk
keyFindings: Gingival redness, swelling, and bleeding on light provocation, most pronounced at lower anterior region
Prior periodontal charting (3 years ago) showing 4-5mm pockets with bleeding on probing in molars - overdue for reassessment
HbA1c 8.2%, indicating suboptimal diabetes control, trending upward over 18 months
Amlodipine use with visible gingival enlargement pattern consistent with drug-associated overgrowth

Ineffective home care: once-daily brushing with excessive force/horizontal scrubbing, flossing only when food is stuck (not systematic/daily despite earlier report of daily flossing), daily alcohol-containing mouthwash use
Xerostomia symptoms with frequent sweetened chai sipping throughout the day, raising caries risk
Paan with areca nut use several times monthly, an oral cancer risk factor not previously identified or counseled on
No visible oral mucosal lesions, ulcers, or masses on limited camera exam; no reported loose teeth, jaw pain, or chewing difficulty
plan: Refer to dentist for in-person comprehensive periodontal re-evaluation and updated full-mouth charting given overdue status (3 years) and prior documented 4-5mm pockets

Refer to dentist/physician for evaluation of gingival enlargement to distinguish drug-associated overgrowth from inflammatory swelling and discuss whether an alternate antihypertensive might be considered by her physician (hygienist does not prescribe or change medications)
Communicate findings to patient's primary care physician regarding suboptimal glycemic control (HbA1c 8.2%) and its relationship to periodontal health, encouraging patient to discuss with PCP

Provide oral hygiene instruction: switch to soft-bristled brush, modified Bass or gentle technique, brush twice daily for 2 minutes, add systematic daily interdental cleaning (floss or interdental brush)
Counsel on discontinuing or reducing alcohol-containing mouthwash in setting of xerostomia; consider alcohol-free fluoride rinse
Counsel on dry mouth management strategies (sugar-free hydration, saliva substitutes, reducing frequency of sweetened chai sipping) to lower caries risk

Provide oral cancer risk counseling specifically addressing areca nut/paan use, framed respectfully and non-judgmentally, with clear explanation that this is a modifiable risk factor independent of cigarette smoking
Schedule in-person periodontal maintenance/comprehensive exam with dentist as soon as feasible, given 3-year gap and prior moderate periodontitis findings
Document findings using ADPIED framework and ensure findings needing diagnosis or treatment planning are flagged for the dentist
redFlags: Any oral ulcer, white/red patch, or mass persisting more than 2 weeks would require urgent dental/oral medicine referral for biopsy evaluation given areca nut exposure (not present today but to screen for at every visit)
Loose teeth or rapid attachment loss would suggest advancing periodontitis needing urgent dental evaluation (not present today)
Significant unexplained weight loss, dysphagia, or persistent hoarseness would warrant urgent referral given oral cancer risk factors (not reported today)
educationPoints: Self-reported flossing frequency often does not match actual behavior; clinical signs like bleeding on probing are more objective indicators of home care effectiveness than self-report
Areca nut/paan chewing is an independent oral cancer risk factor regardless of whether tobacco is included, and patients may not recognize it as a 'tobacco' product requiring cessation counseling
Poorly controlled diabetes and periodontal disease have a bidirectional relationship: hyperglycemia worsens periodontal inflammation, and periodontal infection can worsen glycemic control
Amlodipine (a calcium channel blocker) is a recognized cause of gingival overgrowth; patients on this medication with gingival enlargement should have this discussed with their prescribing physician
Alcohol-containing mouthwash can worsen xerostomia symptoms; alcohol-free alternatives are preferable for patients with dry mouth
Brushing harder or with a firm-bristle brush does not clean more effectively and can contribute to gingival trauma and recession over time; gentle technique with a soft brush is recommended

The dental hygienist's role includes risk assessment, education, and prevention counseling, but diagnosis, periodontal charting interpretation for treatment planning, and medication changes remain within the dentist's or physician's scope and should be referred appropriately

profile.title: Bleeding gums and halitosis in a 52-year-old with diabetes and prior periodontal disease
profile.summary: A 52-year-old Indian-American woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 8.2%) and a history of localized moderate periodontitis presents for tele-hygiene assessment of bleeding gums and bad breath. The case teaches oral health risk assessment via telehealth, including camera-guided exam and home care demonstration, recognition of systemic and medication-related contributors to periodontal and caries risk (diabetes, amlodipine-associated gingival overgrowth, xerostomia, frequent sweetened beverage intake), culturally sensitive screening for areca nut/paan as an oral cancer risk, and appropriate referral to the dentist for findings beyond the hygienist's scope.
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit; patient's home office in Edison, New Jersey
